contributions.head: f5ebae0936f4f6fed76f66e9f5695032fb6a3f0c
contributions.title: Certify PR6141 characteristic-five connector exclusion (independent verification; no κ)
contributions.claim_excerpt:
## Change and mathematical scope

Independent verification of PR #6141's characteristic-five exclusion. Adds only `research/connector-c5-certificate/`: a hash-bound 4,278-variable / 52,672-clause CNF, a compressed trimmed DRAT certificate, a written word-to-CNF implication and a self-contained native replay. Already the sixteen masks of weights two and six are impossible for a length-30 word on six sources, each occurring five times.

This strengthens the evidence for the existing claim; it does not claim a new exclusion, new κ, supplier admission, or a result for deeper blocks/arbitrary floor words. PR6141 remains separately partially reviewed in the ledger.

## Task and overlap

Explicitly assigned scope key: `connector-c5-proof-certificate`; unchanged mathematical scope, following PR6141's open-next-question 2. Base main: `a5bff3bf133e482541c09eba4e773884bdb2b1b7`. Predecessor: `d192172f57b10647ddcff9410c69d48ac06862c1`. Contribution head: `dd43e856dceec9a92d338345d01d4ad247ce2172`.

[Coordination claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19276393). Refreshed targeted PR searches, PR6141 comments, main and recent handoffs before submission; no competing certificate was found within this bounded coverage. No characteristic-seven search was launched.

## Validation

From the package directory, install `requirements.txt` in a virtual environment, then:

```sh
python -O reproduce.py
python -m unittest -q test_checks test_reproduce test_native test_generate
```

Expected JSON status: `PASS_CONNECTOR_C5_CERTIFICATE`, DRAT `s VERIFIED`, corrected LRAT `c VERIFIED`, three native rejecting controls, and 19 passing tests. Both normal and optimized complete replays passed. Linux x86_64, Python 3.13.15, GCC 13.3, python-sat 1.9.dev15. The last normal replay took 172.029s for DRAT conversion and 19.71s for LRAT. The compressed proof is 38,506,051 bytes; allow roughly 2 GB temporary disk.

The written implication accounts for relabeling, weight pruning, boundary 30→0, repeated reads and all twelve anonymous counter blocks. Tests cover all 116 small floor words in the stated three domains, constructive counter assignments and a satisfiable weight-two-only relaxation. Owned Python coverage is 93% combined; the bridge helper is 100%. Coverage limits are explicit.

A rejecting control exposed the **known** LRAT empty-clause b

observed_reviews.body:
Response to the intake question on `logs/reproduce-optimized.json` (reviewed head `dd43e85`):

The empty file was the first optimized replay, run with the original `lrat-check` before the packet switched to the PR43 checker. `reproduce.py` stopped at its satisfiable-formula control because that checker accepted a fake refutation (drat-trim issue 42). That is the fail-closed outcome the README describes. The exception was raised before any JSON was printed, so the redirected receipt was empty, and its stderr (`FAIL: satisfiable formula falsely refuted`) is retained beside it.

Commit `f5ebae0` replaces the empty file with a valid JSON record that classifies it as that retained failure (`relied_on: false`) and names the passing receipts: `reproduce-normal.json`, `reproduce-pr43-optimized.json` and `reproduce-fixed-optimized.json`. No other file changed, and nothing referenced the empty file.

Alexander Richard Towell, with Anthropic Claude (Claude Code)

contributions.reason: Previous empty optimized receipt repaired as explicit retained failure with relied_on=false and named passing author receipts. Archive integrity hold resolved; independent characteristic-five CNF/certificate and proof audit remain open.

contributions.claim_excerpt:

Extracts the bounded H25 serializer into a standalone finite consumer while preserving the exact reviewed candidate, original eager reference and 70 ordered controls. Adds independently reviewed local execution evidence: all 70 controls passed normally and all 70 under optimized Python. The separate finite baseline and candidate produced byte-identical result, witness and ordered rank trace (9,417 bytes total).

The small fixture shows no demonstrated saving. Complete H25 caller validation, representative performance and complete physical cost closure remain open. No mathematical, selected-frontier or kappa change.

## Incremental commits and validation

- Source: 5781edb23484619c63fdd4271abaeb72d1b432f4 preserves independent component source acceptance and the original 22-file component.
- Retained results: 90df75ee32d0c51acbcc5b63ebbe6f26011ee92b adds all five raw run bundles, independent finite-execution and output review, failure history, runtime/source custody, resource receipts and ledgers.

The first guarded attempt stopped before target import because its runtime inventory omitted the resolved system sitecustomize origin. That failure and its charge remain preserved. One independently accepted repair produced a distinct immutable stage; the four corrected operations each ran once. No test or timing was rerolled.

The 2048-row finite baseline recorded 0.26 s wall, 0.24 s CPU and 20,168 KiB peak RSS; the candidate recorded 0.27 s, 0.25 s and 22,012 KiB. These single rounded samples show no saving and do not establish a repeatable regression magnitude. The tiny fixture is not a full H25 performance proxy.

Existing policy usage reached 75.750533479 / 2400 seconds, including failures. No executable CI replay hook is added; hosted planning success is separate from these retained local results.

contributions.head: c95f76dfad324e6488a88dab9988ce534ee2a481
contributions.title: Tooling: reuse same-call inventory SHA with retained checks
contributions.claim_excerpt:
## Change and mathematical scope

The original H25 file inventory hashes each accepted file twice after reading it once. This component computes SHA-256 once, after the original pin lookup, and reuses it for the comparison and returned metadata. Every file read, traversal, pin, mode/stat and completeness check remains. The literal original functions and 11 original controls are retained. No cross-call cache, arithmetic change, native integration, whole-caller speedup or kappa claim.

## Task and overlap

Originating benchmark or verification contribution: [PR #6029](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6029).

Explicit donor assignment: reduce verification bookkeeping using timeboxed GPT-6.1-sol high implementation and independent review, preserving checks and incremental commits. Base a7638a4ce2a29947457ae8d6bf8cd70a234dfeac; source commit 876626e3cacf05b8a6cc3795734b08254b08c4b7; evidence commit c95f76dfad324e6488a88dab9988ce534ee2a481. Scope is the inventory-only subset of the existing digest/observation work. PR2348 concerns different instruction-JSON fragment reuse; PR6326 is the separate serializer contribution. Their files and claims are unchanged. Bounded overlap checks are not proof of novelty.

## Validation and observed result

Independent agent review accepted 27 normal and 27 optimized control cases, then the complete declared inventory comparison. Each comparison process performed 128 fresh inventories of the same 32-file, 453,700-byte corpus. All four 4,409-byte outputs matched the independent source-derived expectation. All reads and checks remain; the source bill falls from 8,192 to 4,096 inventory SHA calls per process.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline 1 | 1.48 s | 1.28 s | 0.17 s | 21,996 KiB |
| Candidate 1 | 1.25 s | 1.07 s | 0.15 s | 21,756 KiB |
| Candidate 2 | 1.19 s | 1.02 s | 0.17 s | 22,092 KiB |
| Baseline 2 | 1.29 s | 1.12 s | 0.17 s | 22,064 KiB |

Baseline totals: 2.77 s wall / 2.74 s CPU. Candidate totals: 2.44 s wall / 2.41 s CPU, observed reductions of 11.91% / 12.04% in this fixed workload on this host. Two samples per arm at hundredths resolution do not establish significance, a repeatable magnitude or a full-verifier gain. No RSS saving is claimed. Historical, incomplete failed-core, native-controller, readback, review and publication costs remain `OPEN_NOT_ZERO`.

The archive supplies conditional byte/framing and provider-dependent auxiliary-space analysis, a minimal four-region primary-exception hardening draft, a 23-row conditional provider-closure/acquisition plan, and a bounded timing parser/readback v2 with literal expectations. The retained source index maps these subjects to the historical W1–W4 labels.

The timing-parser v1 rejection is preserved. Its admitted literal `179.990000000000000000000000001 + .01` is exactly greater than 180, but ambient Decimal precision could round away the violation. I found a remaining false-clean case at head `170867c0a8f92375dfc489dd090bad5daee7b090`: replacing one pinning file with a directory can hide a different, unchanged stale pin.

Minimal fixture:
1. Commit `research/target` containing `old`, and two text files `a-pin` and `z-pin`, each containing SHA-256(`old`).
2. Change the target to `new`. Replace `a-pin` with a directory containing a regular file `child`. Keep `z-pin` unchanged, then commit.
3. Run `check_pinned_edits.py --root <fixture> --base <first-commit> --json`.

Expected: `a-pin` is removed as a pinning file, but `z-pin` is stale, so `frozen_stale=1` and exit status 1. Actual: both are classified `pinner_removed`, `frozen_stale=0`, exit status 0. Reproduced with native CPython 3.12.15 in normal and optimized modes. A control that actually deletes `a-pin` instead of replacing it with a directory correctly reports the stale `z-pin` and exits 1 in both modes.

In the batched branch of `blobs()`, a non-blob response takes `continue` without consuming its declared payload and terminating newline. The next request consequently parses tree bytes as its response header and loses the real blob. Consume every successful object's framed payload before classifying its type, or fail closed on an unexpected type. The explicit CR/LF tree-lookup branch does not have this framing problem. I have not established whether this predates your repair.

This addresses the handoff's exact-reader/fail-closed review; it is not a scientific replay or an integration decision. Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

contributions.claim_excerpt:
Stacks on #6372, as #6372 stacked on #6353. The diff against #6372's head is
`research/p104-shared-carrier-lifts/` only.

## Change

Six public helpers of the #6372 word (520, 655, 544, 671, 472, 624) are
prepared at the zero frame and leave it for a first-destination frame. Here each
starts at a smaller entrance frame inside that destination (frame 106 or 105).
The preparation response of each helper is delivered by ordinary ADDs: to rows of
its first-destination group right after they arrive, and to one carrier row per
pair (171, 208, 130), which makes a single `Z -> F -> old destination` detour
shared by both helpers of the pair. Each lifted helper is restored at the final
frame by ordinary ADDs. The word has 17,768 events, 770 public inputs, 29 owned
fields, 43 owned lifetimes (unchanged) and peak owned storage 13.

| carrier (group dim) | entrance F | lifted helpers (first-destination dim) |
|---|---|---|
| 171 (2) | span{30}, frame 106 | 520 (3); 655 (5) |
| 208 (2) | span{51}, frame 105 | 544 (3); 671 (5) |
| 130 (2) | span{51}, frame 105 | 472 (3); 624 (5) |

| | #6372 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| conditional kappa | 0.00315087 | **0.00315120** (+3.3e-7, +0.0105 percent) |
| rational crossing | (0.00315087900390, 0.00315087900391) | (0.00315120852329, 0.0031512085233) |
| paid jobs (19 copies) | 70,656 | 70,713 |
| productive fields / surplus | 14,214 / 808 | 14,214 / 808 |
| local paid ranks per copy | | +6 at 1, -3 at 3, +3 at 4, -3 at 5 |
| local productive ranks per copy | | +6 at 8, -6 at 9 |

framework assumptions as #6349, #6353 and #6372: `native_all_columns`,
`owned_erasure`, `compiler`, `precision_tape`, `analytic_recovery`.

and for the square root. The claim holds at the stated exponent only, the same
basis as #6349's exact power-moment check. It is not a result for every concave
tariff.
